claims.statement: The definitive CBAM regime creates a recurring importer decision about certificate exposure, declaration readiness, and whether verified actual emissions justify their additional collection and assurance cost.
Evidence supports buyer use of external CBAM data solutions, but price tolerance and the responsible budget owner for the redesigned importer-side decision service remain unvalidated.

The business can propose a direct importer workflow-integration agreement for importer-supplied shipment data and exposure analysis while treating supplier actual-emissions evidence as optional; no such agreement or customer right is presently held.

A standardized diagnostic and monitoring subscription should require less supplier-operations labor than the original managed data desk, but realized acquisition cost, delivery cost, margin, retention, and payback remain unknown and face a low-priced software benchmark.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Finance, customs, tax, or trade-compliance director; actual owner is unvalidated
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: The service is not protected from bundling; resistance depends on producing a faster independent default-versus-actual value case and an importer-owned audit trail without replacing the broker, ERP, registry, or accredited verifier
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with in-scope EU importers
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Founder-controlled targeted outreach to in-scope importers, supplemented by nonexclusive accountant, customs-adviser, and trade-association referrals

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Unvalidated target: 3,000-10,000 PLN per won importer using narrow outbound lists and referral fees; measure labor, list cost, meetings, sales-cycle length, and commissions before scaling
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Proposed diagnostic paid 50% at order and 50% on delivery; monitoring subscription billed quarterly or annually in advance; verifier and specialist pass-through work requires customer prepayment
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target: 55-75% on standardized diagnostics and monitoring before fixed overhead; reject or reprice accounts whose data cleanup, specialist review, or support hours breach the quoted labor allowance
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Model assumption: 12-30 founder or analyst hours for initial importer-data mapping and 2-6 hours per month for exception monitoring; actual time, language burden, and defect rates must be measured
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Budget for legal terms, data-processing controls, cybersecurity, professional-liability cover, regulatory-content maintenance, bookkeeping, and independent carbon-methodology review; accredited verification remains separately procured when actual values are used
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Fixed-fee default-versus-actual exposure and readiness diagnostic, followed by a quarterly or annual importer-side monitoring subscription; supplier chasing and verification are optional prepaid add-ons
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Analyst data normalization, limited customer support, referral commission, specialist review, and any customer-approved verifier or supplier-escalation work; no open-ended supplier outreach is included in the base fee

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: CBAM software vendors, customs brokers, and SAP are likely to add exposure comparisons and bundle them with filing or ERP workflows; the business must remain integration-neutral, show quantified time or certificate-value improvement, and avoid competing on generic record collection
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Importer certificate cash exposure, internal preparation labor, and the avoidable cost of collecting and verifying actual values when Commission defaults are economically preferable
commercial_mechanics.payer: In-scope EU importer with material CBAM certificate exposure; willingness to pay and exact budget owner remain unknown
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: First certificate forecast, annual declaration preparation, a material change in EU ETS-linked exposure, or a decision whether supplier actual values justify collection and accredited verification
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Quarterly exposure refresh and annual CBAM declaration cycle, conditional on continuing imports and demonstrated decision or labor value

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne exemption removes the vast majority of importers and concentrates the addressable market in fewer, larger accounts.
A direct substitute offers supplier evidence requests, audit history, regulatory export, and broker white-labelling at £199-£699 per month.
SAP can bundle customs, ERP, supplier-emissions, calculation, reporting, and financial-liability workflows.
Commission default values make supplier-level actual-data collection nonessential in some cases.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive workflow-integration and service agreement granting access to importer-controlled shipment records, authority to produce exposure analyses, and a direct paid customer interface; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a fixed-fee offline diagnostic using customer-exported shipment data and public default-value rules; if the importer will not contract or supply exports, do not launch that account and pursue another in-scope importer
critical_control_point.current_owner: Importers control their shipment records and buying decision; the prospective business presently holds no workflow integration or customer contract
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with in-scope EU importers
critical_control_point.duration: Unknown until signed; proposed 12-month term for monitoring and a fixed delivery term for the diagnostic
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No importer workflow right or direct customer contract is presently held; the founder can build the analytical method from lawful public rules and customer-provided exports without employer resources
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The prospective business controls the offer, analysis workflow, pricing, and account acceptance after an importer signs; the importer controls data disclosure and the regulatory filing
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed annual renewal for monitoring; unsigned and unvalidated
critical_control_point.subject: Direct importer exposure-decision workflow and paid customer interface

economics.acquisition_route: Target a manually researched list of in-scope importers with a fixed-scope paid exposure diagnostic; require payment and a customer data export before building integrations, then test conversion to monitoring through direct contracts and nonexclusive adviser referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: reach 100 importers averaging 30,000 PLN annual recurring revenue for 3m PLN ARR, then 200 importers for 6m PLN ARR; at a 20-30% owner-earnings margin with retained equity and limited distributions while employed, 5m PLN founder net worth could be plausible in roughly 7-10 years. This path fails if direct CAC, support labor, renewal, or pricing do not support contribution profit and no valuation multiple is assumed as guaranteed.
economics.founder_time: 15-25 hours weekly for the initial diagnostic and automation phase; cap concurrent accounts and hire contract analyst capacity only after prepaid work demonstrates positive contribution
economics.gross_margin_basis: Diagnostic and subscription revenue less analyst delivery, support, referral commissions, specialist review, and customer-specific processing; verifier fees and exceptional supplier work are prepaid pass-throughs rather than absorbed margin
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: acquisition spend recovered from diagnostic contribution or within six subscription months; stop the channel if a cohort does not recover fully loaded CAC within 12 months
economics.pricing: Test 6,000-15,000 PLN per diagnostic and 1,500-4,000 PLN per month for monitoring, with explicit data-volume and support limits; competitor software pricing makes the upper range contingent on measurable managed decision value
economics.retention_or_repeat: Quarterly exposure monitoring and annual declaration preparation; renewal is unproven and should be measured by paid second-cycle continuation rather than assumed regulatory recurrence

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable importer exposure models, default-versus-actual decision benchmarks, and integration mappings built only from data the business may lawfully retain
fingerprint.customer: In-scope EU importers with material CBAM certificate exposure
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Founder-controlled account outreach plus nonexclusive accountant, customs-adviser, and trade-association referrals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fixed-fee CBAM exposure diagnostic plus importer-side monitoring subscription with prepaid specialist add-ons
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays to quantify certificate exposure and decide whether actual supplier data and verification are worth their cost
fingerprint.problem_trigger: CBAM moved from transitional reporting to certificate-bearing definitive operation

founder_fit: Data validation and financial modeling fit the founder's skills.
The standardized diagnostic can begin part-time without owning supplier source data or performing regulated verification.
Founder-controlled targeted outreach reduces reliance on brokers while allowing nonexclusive referrals.
The workflow can be automated only after paid cases reveal repeatable data mappings and support load.

redesign.economic_effect: The redesign removes open-ended supplier collection from the base offer and replaces supplier cooperation as the critical mechanism with a contractible importer-side decision workflow. Fixed-scope diagnostics, capped support, advance billing, and prepaid verifier or specialist add-ons reduce delivery variance and working-capital exposure; direct acquisition may improve relationship control but its CAC, price, conversion, margins, and renewal remain unvalidated.

risks: Importers may prefer default values, broker bundles, low-priced software, or SAP and decline a separate service.
No direct importer contract, referral agreement, workflow right, or validated acquisition channel exists today.
Actual delivery hours, data quality, CAC, price tolerance, insurance cost, contribution margin, and renewal are unknown.
Regulatory or methodology mistakes could create liability even though accredited verification is not offered.
The narrowed market may produce enterprise sales cycles incompatible with part-time founder capacity.
Reusable customer data and benchmarks may be contractually restricted, limiting compounding advantage.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: fixed scope cbam exposure diagnostic and importer monitoring subscription
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: direct importer exposure decision workflow under a proposed service and integration agreement
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: in scope importer willingness to contract provide shipment exports and renew

structure.commercial_archetype: Productized regulatory exposure diagnostic with recurring monitoring
structure.control_point: Direct importer contract and embedded exposure-decision workflow
structure.critical_dependency: Importer adoption and permissioned shipment-data access; supplier actual-emissions data is optional

thesis: CBAM's certificate-bearing operation creates a paid importer-side decision about exposure and whether verified actual values justify their collection cost; a fixed-scope decision workflow can avoid dependence on owning supplier measurements, verifier accreditation, or the official registry.
title: CBAM Exposure Decision Desk
uncertainties: The number, spend, and sales-cycle length of addressable regional importers above the threshold remain unknown.
No evidence establishes diagnostic price tolerance, direct conversion, CAC, delivery hours, contribution margin, or renewal.
It is unknown how often actual values produce enough certificate savings or commercial benefit to change an importer's decision.
Proposed importer workflow agreements, data rights, retention rights, and referral terms are unsigned.
Insurance, cybersecurity, specialist-review, and regulatory-maintenance costs remain unknown.
It is unknown whether lawful retained mappings and benchmarks create switching costs or defensibility against bundled incumbents.
